textos.txt: The trees whisper about samples collected without a plan, without a method, without purpose
When sampling is careless, even the forest loses its harmony
So, a poorly done collection can affect the entire analysis?
I thought it was just about grabbing a handful of leaves and that’s it...
Ah, if only it were that simple…
Without traceability, your data scatter like leaves in the wind
A sample without a plan is like a seed cast in barren soil — it never grows into reliable results
Let’s see if you can collect with the same care the standard requires
Which of the following alternatives represents a **nonconformity** with the sampling requirements according to ISO/IEC 17025?

alternativas.txt: The laboratory prepares a sampling plan when it is responsible for this activity, considering appropriate technical and statistical criteria.
Sampling records include the sample identification, date, location, responsible person, and method used, ensuring traceability.
Technicians perform sampling based solely on their experience, without formal documentation, as this speeds up the process.
The laboratory uses documented procedures to ensure that samples adequately represent the original batch.
The sampling plan is reviewed and adjusted as needed according to technical requirements or client changes.

Likewise, a solid sampling plan sustains reliable results
